presentingComplaint: Progressive confusion, polyuria and constipation over 10 days in a woman with metastatic breast cancer, type 2 diabetes and CKD.
history: 68-year-old woman with oestrogen-receptor-positive breast cancer treated 3 years ago, now with known bone metastases (spine, pelvis) on an aromatase inhibitor. Comorbid type 2 diabetes (metformin, on background of stage 3b CKD; baseline creatinine ~1.6 mg/dL) and hypertension. Over 10 days she has become increasingly lethargic, low in mood and confused, with polyuria, marked thirst, anorexia, nausea, constipation and generalised bony/back pain. Family note reduced oral intake and two falls. Because of the diabetes and CKD, symptoms were initially attributed to poor glycaemic control and worsening renal function, but random glucose was only modestly raised and ketones negative. No fever, cough, dysuria or focal infective symptoms. Not taking calcium/vitamin D supplements or thiazides.
examination: Drowsy but rousable, oriented to person only. Clinically dehydrated: dry mucous membranes, reduced skin turgor, sunken eyes. Abdomen soft with sluggish bowel sounds and palpable faecal loading; no peritonism. Tender lower thoracic/lumbar spine on percussion. No neck stiffness, no focal neurological deficit, reflexes reduced. Chest clear, no signs of infection or heart failure.
imaging: CT/plain films confirm lytic and sclerotic metastatic deposits in thoracic/lumbar vertebrae and pelvis. Renal tract normal, no obstruction. No new pulmonary lesion. Skeletal disease consistent with progressive bony metastatic breast cancer.
microbiology: Not indicated; no clinical evidence of infection. Blood/urine cultures not sent.
differentialDiagnoses: Hypercalcaemia of malignancy (humoral PTHrP-mediated + osteolytic bone metastases)
Multiple myeloma (excluded - no monoclonal band, imaging fits breast metastases)
Hyperosmolar hyperglycaemic state (glucose only modestly raised, ketones negative)
Uraemic/metabolic encephalopathy from AKI-on-CKD (contributory but does not explain hypercalcaemia)
finalDiagnosis: Severe hypercalcaemia of malignancy in metastatic breast cancer, with dehydration-driven AKI on background CKD and confounding type 2 diabetes
citations: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e - Hypercalcemia and Disorders of Calcium Homeostasis
stewardship: Not applicable - non-infective metabolic emergency. Management priorities: aggressive isotonic saline rehydration with careful monitoring given CKD and volume status, IV bisphosphonate (zoledronic acid, dose-adjusted for renal function) or denosumab if bisphosphonate contraindicated by eGFR, calcitonin for rapid short-term lowering, hold nephrotoxins and calcium/vitamin D, review causative oncological therapy, and treat the underlying malignancy.
contraindications: Loop diuretics only after euvolaemia restored, not for routine calcium-lowering
Zoledronic acid caution/dose reduction with eGFR <30-35; consider denosumab instead
Avoid calcium- or vitamin D-containing supplements
Avoid nephrotoxins (NSAIDs, contrast) given AKI on CKD
edgeCases: CKD raises baseline creatinine, masking the acuity of dehydration-driven AKI
Diabetes-related polyuria/thirst can be mistaken for poor glycaemic control, delaying calcium testing
Low albumin means total calcium underestimates true burden - corrected/ionised calcium essential
Renal impairment limits bisphosphonate choice and dosing
expectedMaiK: In a patient with metastatic malignancy presenting with confusion, polyuria, constipation and dehydration, check corrected/ionised calcium early; suppressed PTH with elevated PTHrP and known bone metastases confirms hypercalcaemia of malignancy - CKD and diabetes are confounders, not the primary cause.
expectedNextQuestions: Any calcium/vitamin D supplements, thiazides or lithium?
Baseline renal function and usual creatinine?
Progression of the underlying cancer and current oncological treatment?
Fluid intake, urine output and recent weight change?
Symptoms of infection or other cause of altered sensorium?
expectedInvestigations: Phosphate, magnesium, renal profile and eGFR
Serum/urine protein electrophoresis and free light chains to exclude myeloma

investigations: Serum/urine protein electrophoresis with free light chains

regressionAssertions: Engine must rank hypercalcemia as the top diagnosis
Suppressed PTH with elevated PTHrP and bone metastases should point to hypercalcaemia of malignancy, not primary hyperparathyroidism
Elevated glucose with negative ketones and only modest hyperglycaemia should not be classified as HHS/DKA as the primary diagnosis
Management must include IV isotonic fluids and an antiresorptive agent with renal dose consideration, and must not recommend antibiotics
